title: Use parameterized queries everywhere
description: Build every database query by passing user input as a separate parameter, never by string concatenation or template-string interpolation. This works for SQL (pg, mysql2), MongoDB (operator filters), and document DBs. Even ORM helpers can leak via raw query escape hatches — audit those.

examples.safe: db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = $1', [email]);

title: Hash passwords with argon2id or bcrypt — never raw SHA/MD5
description: Password hashes must be slow, salted, and memory-hard to resist offline brute-force. Use argon2id (preferred) or bcrypt with a work factor of 12+. Verify with constant-time compare functions provided by the library.

title: Verify JWTs — algorithm AND signature
description: Always call jwt.verify (not jwt.decode), pin the allowed algorithms list, and reject tokens with `alg: none`. Use HS256 with a 256-bit-plus secret stored in env, or RS256/ES256 with proper key management.

examples.safe: const payload = jwt.verify(token, SECRET, { algorithms: ['HS256'], maxAge: '7d' });

title: Set SameSite=Lax + Secure on all auth cookies
description: Cross-site requests should not carry session cookies for most apps. SameSite=Lax is the right default; Strict is even tighter but breaks some legitimate cross-site links. Always pair with Secure (HTTPS only) and HttpOnly (no JS access).

title: Use helmet to set baseline security headers
description: Standard headers — Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, Referrer-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options — add layered defense against XSS, clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and information leaks. Helmet ships a sensible baseline for Express.

examples.safe:
import helmet from 'helmet';
app.use(helmet({ contentSecurityPolicy: { directives: { ... } } }));

title: Never call eval / new Function / setTimeout(string) on user input
description: These all parse arbitrary code at runtime. There is no safe way to use them with attacker-influenced strings. For configurable expressions, write a small parser or use a library with an explicit scope (mathjs, expr-eval).

examples.safe:
import { evaluate } from 'mathjs';
const r = evaluate(userFormula, { /* scope */ });

title: Sanitize HTML before dangerouslySetInnerHTML
description: If you must render user-supplied HTML (markdown output, comments), pipe it through DOMPurify with a strict allowlist of tags and attributes. Better: render as text via JSX expressions ({content}). React's automatic escaping handles the common case.

title: Load secrets from environment, never source
description: Hardcoded keys, tokens, and passwords leak the moment the repo is cloned, archived, or breached. Use process.env for runtime configuration; commit only .env.example with placeholder values. Use a secret manager (AWS Secrets Manager, Vault) for production.

examples.safe:
const STRIPE = process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY;
if (!STRIPE) throw new Error('STRIPE_SECRET_KEY missing');

title: Validate redirect targets against an allowlist
description: Open redirects power phishing. Allow only relative paths on your own domain, or absolute URLs whose host is in a small allowlist. Never reflect req.query.url directly into res.redirect.

examples.safe:
const next = String(req.query.next ?? '/');
res.redirect(/^\/[^/]/.test(next) ? next : '/');

title: Rate-limit auth endpoints
description: Login, password-reset, OTP, and signup flows are the primary brute-force targets. Use express-rate-limit (or your gateway's equivalent) keyed by IP + username. Don't rate-limit by IP alone — credential-stuffing attacks rotate IPs cheaply.

title: CORS allowlist — never reflect arbitrary origins with credentials
description: Setting Access-Control-Allow-Origin: req.headers.origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true is equivalent to having no CORS at all. Maintain an explicit allowlist of origins; use a function to validate.

title: Defend against prototype pollution when merging objects
description: Object.assign, lodash.merge, and similar APIs can introduce __proto__ writes when the source is attacker-controlled. Use Object.create(null) as the target, or explicitly copy only known keys. Recent lodash versions guard against this — older ones do not.

title: Avoid NoSQL operator injection
description: Mongoose / MongoDB queries built from req.body are vulnerable if the request contains MongoDB operators ({$ne: null}, {$gt: ''}). Cast inputs to expected primitive types before using them in filters, or use a schema validator that rejects nested objects.

examples.vulnerable:
// req.body.email = { $ne: null } → matches every user
User.findOne({ email: req.body.email });
examples.safe:
const email = String(req.body.email);
User.findOne({ email });

title: Verify ownership of every resource — not just authentication
description: requireAuth tells you WHO is calling. It does NOT tell you whether THIS user is allowed to access THIS resource. Every resource handler must check that the resource belongs to req.user (or that the user has the required role).

title: Validate file uploads — MIME, size, AND magic bytes
description: Trusting the client-supplied Content-Type or extension is naive. Use a library that sniffs the actual file header (file-type), enforce size limits at multer/busboy level, and serve uploads from an isolated origin or via signed URLs so they can't access your site's cookies.

title: Constant-time compare for tokens & HMACs
description: String equality (===) and Buffer.compare leak length and early-mismatch timing, which can be measured remotely to recover secrets byte by byte. Use crypto.timingSafeEqual for any sensitive comparison.

title: Don't leak stack traces or internal error messages in prod
description: Detailed errors are gold for attackers — they reveal stack frames, DB types, file paths, library versions. Set an error handler that returns a generic message in production while still logging the full stack server-side.

title: Enforce input length and shape limits
description: Reject oversized bodies and pathologically nested JSON before they reach business logic. Use express.json({ limit: '1mb' }) (or smaller for most routes), Zod / Joi schemas for body validation, and a global timeout for slow clients.

title: Don't store sensitive data in localStorage
description: localStorage is readable by any JavaScript running on the page — including injected XSS payloads, malicious dependencies, browser extensions. For session credentials prefer httpOnly cookies. If you must use localStorage (e.g. portfolio app convenience), ensure aggressive CSP and accept the XSS-equivalent compromise.

examples.safe:
// Backend sets the cookie:
res.cookie('session', token, { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: 'lax' });

title: Pin and audit dependencies; act on `npm audit` / OSV.dev findings
description: Use exact versions or tight semver in package.json. Run `npm audit` (or Snyk / GitHub Dependabot) in CI and fail builds on high/critical findings. For transitive vulnerabilities you can't upgrade, use `overrides` in package.json to force a patched version.

examples.vulnerable: // package.json with floating major and no audit gate
